note: THE SIGN FLIP MEASURED DIRECTLY - the exact question Ruling 1 said makes this one chapter. But NOT identified: cross-country aggregate panel, endogeneity tested for GDP and FLFP only, no instrument for credit. Secondary pool per the scope memo's rule on aggregate designs.

estimate: interaction negative in sign but economically small and statistically INSIGNIFICANT
SETTING_FINANCE_DEPTH: banks per county, time-varying; irrigation and machinery also measured

An UNINFORMATIVE null, not a precise zero: the author writes it is 'hard to say whether financial services could not or were not used for risk coping or whether the available measures of access to financial services are simply too crude'. Record it as imprecise, not as evidence of no effect. NOTE the contrast within the same table: the irrigation and machinery interactions DO attenuate the buffer effect, so risk-mitigating TECHNOLOGY works where the financial-access measure does not.

study: The Babies of Mortgage Market Deregulation (a.k.a. The Babies of Financial Deregulation)
exposure: mortgage market deregulation - a US federal regulator ruling creating geographic heterogeneity in access to mortgage credit
note: SECOND IDENTIFIED ESTIMATE. ONE STUDY IN THREE VERSIONS: 'The Babies of Financial Deregulation' (SSRN 2016), this SSRN working paper (2020) and the RFS article - all Isaac Hacamo, same regulator-ruling design. Do not count more than once. Author's supplemental tests REJECT income and housing-wealth channels and point to ACCESS TO SPACE as the mechanism - which sits on the C.2.c boundary (space is a housing attribute) even though the varying object is credit. Sign POSITIVE, Arm B's direction.

study: Do Mortgage Interest Subsidies Affect Fertility and Housing Purchase Decisions?
exposure: preferential mortgage rates / mortgage interest deduction scheme
estimate: NO effect on fertility (first stage verified: mortgage burden -7.9%, and -17.6% outside the most expensive cities)
source: ABSTRACT (full text on the residual retrieval list)
note: THIRD IDENTIFIED ARM B ESTIMATE AND THE FIRST IDENTIFIED NULL. It is an INFORMATIVE null - the policy demonstrably cut mortgage burden by 7.9%, so the zero on fertility is not a failed first stage. Contrast with the two positive identified estimates: those are credit-SUPPLY/access shocks (extensive margin - can you borrow), this is a COST reduction for people already borrowing (intensive margin). That distinction may be the reconciliation. Numbers are abstract-sourced.

study: Credit Availability, Intergenerational Interactions and Family Fertility Decisions
estimate: INVERTED-U: credit expansion raises fertility up to a point, then lowers it; marginal effect heterogeneous in household structure
source: ABSTRACT (full text on the residual retrieval list)
note: Fixed-effects Poisson + IV on China Family Panel Studies 2018-2022. A WITHIN-SETTING nonlinearity, distinct from the cross-setting sign flip in the aggregate panel - but the same theme: the sign of the credit effect depends on where on the curve a setting sits. Also reports bequests raising fertility INTENTIONS via liquidity and educational investment suppressing fertility via quantity-quality - different OUTCOME_LEVEL, record separately at full text. Numbers are abstract-sourced.
